project.name: react-socket-link
project.description: Typed WebSocket connection management for React 18+ and standalone TypeScript, where a socket definition fixes incoming and outgoing message types. Logical connections keep their identity, state, queue, and subscriptions while replaceable native WebSockets handle transport, and a react-free core entry point is exposed.

nodes.name: ConnectionDefinition.ts
nodes.summary: Declares the BaseMessage contract and the SocketDefinition identity/type token, plus defineSocket to create frozen, symbol-identified definitions that never open a socket.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses an optional phantom function-typed property (__messages) to make Incoming/Outgoing generics invariant so distinct protocols cannot be interchanged.

nodes.name: defineSocket
nodes.summary: Validates a non-empty name and returns a frozen SocketDefinition carrying a unique Symbol id typed with incoming/outgoing message generics.

nodes.name: ConnectionState.ts
nodes.summary: Defines connection status and error-code union types, the SocketError and ConnectionSnapshot shapes, and a snapshot factory for immutable state objects.

nodes.name: snapshot
nodes.summary: Builds a frozen ConnectionSnapshot from status, reconnect attempt and last error, deriving isConnected from OPEN status.

nodes.name: LogicalConnection.ts
nodes.summary: Core logical connection implementation: a stable identity that owns retry policy, outgoing queue, message/state subscriptions and open-waiters while swapping replaceable WebSocketTransport instances underneath. Also defines the SocketView/SocketController interfaces and the createSocket factory.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a monotonically increasing generation counter plus queueMicrotask coalescing to ignore stale transport callbacks and avoid allocating sockets for superseded attempts; arrow-function class fields keep getSnapshot/subscribeState referentially stable for useSyncExternalStore.

nodes.name: LogicalConnection
nodes.summary: Stateful connection controller implementing SocketController: manages connect/reconnect/update/close/dispose lifecycle, exponential-backoff retries, a bounded send queue flushed on open, typed per-message-type subscriptions, state listeners and whenOpen promises.

nodes.name: createSocket
nodes.summary: Factory that constructs a new LogicalConnection for a definition and options.

nodes.name: SocketProvider.tsx
nodes.summary: React context provider that eagerly creates a registry of LogicalConnections from socket registrations, connects them on mount, and disposes them on unmount in a Strict-Mode-safe way; also exposes registerSocket and useProviderSocket.
nodes.languageNotes: Deferred disposal via queueMicrotask plus a lifecycle version ref lets the Strict Mode double effect invocation reuse the same instances instead of destroying them.

nodes.name: registerSocket
nodes.summary: Typed helper that pairs a socket definition with matching options so types are bound before erasure in a heterogeneous registration list.

nodes.name: SocketProvider
nodes.summary: Provider component building a symbol-keyed registry of logical connections (rejecting duplicates), connecting all on mount and closing then conditionally disposing them on cleanup.

nodes.name: useProviderSocket
nodes.summary: Hook that reads the provider registry and returns the LogicalConnection registered for a definition, throwing if the provider or registration is missing.

nodes.name: useGlobalSocket.ts
nodes.summary: Hook returning the read/send SocketView of a provider-registered global socket for a given definition.

nodes.name: useGlobalSocket
nodes.summary: Returns the provider-managed connection narrowed to the SocketView interface (send, subscribe, state, whenOpen).

nodes.name: useGlobalSocketController.ts
nodes.summary: Hook returning the full SocketController (connect/reconnect/update/close) for a provider-registered global socket.

nodes.name: useGlobalSocketController
nodes.summary: Returns the provider-managed connection typed as a SocketController, granting lifecycle control to the caller.

nodes.name: useSocketEvent.ts
nodes.summary: Hook subscribing a handler to a typed message type (or wildcard) on a socket, keeping the latest handler in a ref to avoid resubscription.

nodes.name: useSocketEvent
nodes.summary: Subscribes to messages of a given type via socket.subscribe in an effect, forwarding to the latest handler stored in a ref and unsubscribing on cleanup.

nodes.name: useSocketSend.ts
nodes.summary: Hook producing a memoized send function bound to a socket.

nodes.name: useSocketSend
nodes.summary: Returns a useCallback-memoized function that sends an outgoing message through the socket and yields its SendResult.

nodes.name: useSocketState.ts
nodes.summary: Hook exposing a socket's ConnectionSnapshot to React via useSyncExternalStore.

nodes.name: useSocketState
nodes.summary: Binds socket.subscribeState and getSnapshot to useSyncExternalStore for tear-free connection state reads.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: React-free '/core' entry point barrel that re-exports socket definitions, the LogicalConnection/createSocket API, option and state types, and backoff helpers for standalone TypeScript use.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses inline `type` modifiers in re-export lists so type-only symbols are erased under isolatedModules.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Main package entry point that re-exports the full public API: core connection primitives and types plus the React SocketProvider, registerSocket, and socket hooks.

nodes.name: core.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for LogicalConnection behavior: identity preservation across transport replacement, update coalescing, reconnection/backoff, queue bounding and flushing, readiness waits, update validation with credential redaction, heartbeats, and codec rejection.

nodes.name: MockWebSocket.ts
nodes.summary: Test double for the browser WebSocket built on EventTarget, tracking created instances, sent payloads and close calls, with helpers to simulate open, message and abnormal close events.

nodes.name: MockWebSocket
nodes.summary: EventTarget-based fake WebSocket stubbed globally in tests; records every instance and sent message and exposes open(), message(), and fail() to drive transport lifecycle events.

nodes.name: react.test.tsx
nodes.summary: React integration tests verifying global sockets start without consumers and share one controller, local socket identity across re-renders and key changes, Strict Mode effect replay safety, and independent connections per hook owner.

nodes.name: types.test.ts
nodes.summary: Compile-time type tests using expectTypeOf and @ts-expect-error to ensure socket definitions bind incoming/outgoing message types, narrow subscribed events, and reject mismatched codecs or sends.
nodes.languageNotes: Relies on `@ts-expect-error` inside dead `if (false)` branches so invalid calls are type-checked but never executed.

nodes.name: ConnectionOptions.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the typed socket configuration surface (SocketOptions, heartbeat/reconnect/queue options, MessageCodec, patch type) plus the default JSON codec and runtime validation/merging of options.
nodes.languageNotes: Generic interfaces parameterized by Incoming/Outgoing message types; SocketOptionsPatch uses Partial/Omit with nullable heartbeat to allow explicit removal.

nodes.name: ReconnectionPolicy.ts
nodes.summary: Declares the BackoffStrategy type: a function mapping a one-based retry attempt to a delay in milliseconds.

nodes.name: WebSocketTransport.ts
nodes.summary: Wraps a single native WebSocket with an immutable handshake configuration, forwarding open/message/error/close events and managing heartbeat pings and silence timeouts; disposable so retired sockets never call back.
nodes.languageNotes: Arrow-function class properties keep stable listener references so addEventListener/removeEventListener pair correctly.

nodes.name: useLocalSocket.ts
nodes.summary: React hook that creates a component-scoped logical socket via createSocket, connecting on mount and closing/disposing on unmount with StrictMode-safe deferred disposal.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a WeakMap lifecycle version counter plus queueMicrotask so StrictMode double-mount does not dispose a socket that was immediately remounted.

nodes.name: Backoff.ts
nodes.summary: Provides reconnection BackoffStrategy factories: exponential backoff with full jitter and a fixed-delay strategy.

nodes.name: validateOptions
nodes.summary: Validates SocketOptions at runtime: ws/wss URL, protocols shape, positive heartbeat/queue numbers, reconnect maxAttempts, backoff and codec function types, throwing descriptive errors.

nodes.name: mergeOptions
nodes.summary: Merges a SocketOptionsPatch into current options, deep-merging heartbeat/reconnect/queue (null removes heartbeat), then validates the result.

nodes.name: WebSocketTransport
nodes.summary: Owns one native WebSocket: connect, send, dispose, event forwarding to TransportEvents, and heartbeat interval/silence-timeout handling that closes with code 4000 on failure.

nodes.name: useLocalSocket
nodes.summary: Memoizes a SocketController keyed by definition and optional key, connects in an effect, and on cleanup closes then disposes only if no newer lifecycle took over.

nodes.name: exponentialBackoff
nodes.summary: Returns a BackoffStrategy computing random(0, min(cap, base*2^(attempt-1))) to avoid thundering-herd reconnects.

nodes.name: fixedBackoff
nodes.summary: Returns a BackoffStrategy that always yields the same delay; useful for tests or LAN apps.

nodes.name: LICENSE.md
nodes.summary: MIT license text granting permissive reuse rights for the react-socket-link package; shipped in the npm tarball via package.json "files".

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Project documentation for react-socket-link v1.0 covering install, typed protocol definitions with defineSocket, global Provider-based and local hook-based React connections, the standalone /core createSocket API, options (heartbeat, reconnect backoff, queue, codec), state snapshots, and a migration guide from v0.1.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: npm manifest for react-socket-link 1.0.0: dual ESM/CJS exports for the root (React) entry and a React-free "./core" subpath, optional React >=18 peer dependency, and Vite/Vitest/tsc build, test and typecheck scripts.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the "exports" map with types/import/require conditions plus peerDependenciesMeta to make React optional for the core subpath.

nodes.name: tsconfig.app.json
nodes.summary: Vite-template TypeScript config for application sources in src: ES2023 + DOM, bundler module resolution, react-jsx, verbatimModuleSyntax and erasableSyntaxOnly with no emit.

nodes.name: tsconfig.build.json
nodes.summary: Build-only TypeScript config extending tsconfig.json that emits declaration files to dist/ for the published library sources (src/index.ts, src/core, src/react, Backoff) while excluding tests.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: Root TypeScript configuration used for editor IntelliSense and typechecking: strict ES2020/DOM settings with bundler resolution and react-jsx, covering src, tests, examples and Vite/Vitest configs.

nodes.name: tsconfig.node.json
nodes.summary: TypeScript configuration for Node-side tooling, scoped to vite.config.ts with ES2023 target, Node types and bundler resolution.

nodes.name: .npmrc
nodes.summary: npm client configuration holding an authentication entry for the public npm registry, used when publishing the react-socket-link package. Contains a credential and should not be committed or shared.
nodes.languageNotes: A registry-scoped auth token line in .npmrc lets `npm publish` authenticate without an interactive login; such files are normally gitignored or use an environment-variable reference instead of a literal token.

nodes.name: eslint.config.js
nodes.summary: ESLint flat config that lints all TypeScript/TSX sources with the recommended JS, typescript-eslint, React Hooks and React Refresh (Vite) rule sets using browser globals, ignoring the dist output.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the ESLint 9 flat config API (`defineConfig` and `globalIgnores` from `eslint/config`) instead of the legacy .eslintrc format.

nodes.name: vite.config.ts
nodes.summary: Vite library-mode build and Vitest configuration: builds two entry points (main `index` and React-free `core`) as ES and CJS bundles with React externalized, emits type declarations via vite-plugin-dts from tsconfig.build.json, and runs tests in jsdom.
nodes.languageNotes: Multi-entry `build.lib.entry` plus a custom `fileName` produces `index.js/index.cjs` and `core.js/core.cjs`, supporting a subpath export for the standalone core.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: README.md introduces react-socket-link v1.0: typed WebSocket connection management for React 18+ and standalone TypeScript. It walks through typed protocol definitions with defineSocket, global Provider-based and local hook-based React connections, the React-free /core createSocket API, and options such as heartbeat, reconnect backoff, queueing and codecs. Keep its central idea in mind for the whole tour: a logical connection keeps identity, state, queue and subscriptions while replaceable native WebSockets do the transport.

tour.title: Two Public Entry Points
tour.description: The package exposes two barrels. src/index.ts is the main entry that re-exports everything, core primitives plus the React SocketProvider, registerSocket and hooks, while src/core/index.ts is the React-free '/core' subpath for standalone TypeScript. package.json wires these up as dual ESM/CJS exports with React as an optional peer dependency, so non-React consumers never pull React in.
tour.languageLesson: Barrel files re-export symbols from many modules (export { x } from './y') to form a curated public API. Combined with the package.json 'exports' map, each subpath (e.g. 'react-socket-link/core') becomes a separate, independently importable entry.

tour.title: Typed Socket Definitions
tour.description: ConnectionDefinition.ts is the most depended-upon file in the project: nearly every core and React module imports it. It declares the BaseMessage contract and the SocketDefinition identity/type token, and defineSocket creates frozen, symbol-identified definitions that never open a socket. Separating 'what a socket speaks' from 'a live connection' lets the same definition be reused by the Provider, local hooks and the core API.
tour.languageLesson: A definition object that carries only type parameters (a 'type token' or phantom type) lets TypeScript bind incoming and outgoing message unions to a value at compile time, even though the runtime object holds no messages. Using a unique Symbol for identity means two definitions never collide, even if they look alike.

tour.title: Options, State and Retry Contracts
tour.description: Building on the definitions from Step 3, these contracts describe how a connection is configured and observed. ConnectionOptions.ts defines SocketOptions (heartbeat, reconnect, queue, codec), the default JSON codec and runtime validation/merging; ConnectionState.ts defines status and error-code unions plus immutable ConnectionSnapshot objects; ReconnectionPolicy.ts reduces retry policy to a BackoffStrategy function from attempt number to delay. Backoff.ts supplies the concrete strategies: exponential backoff with full jitter and a fixed delay.
tour.languageLesson: Modelling status and error codes as string-literal union types gives exhaustive checking in switch statements. Representing a strategy as a plain function type, rather than a class hierarchy, keeps the reconnection policy trivially swappable and testable.

tour.title: The Logical Connection
tour.description: LogicalConnection.ts is the heart of the library and pulls together everything from Steps 3 and 4. It is a stable identity that owns the retry policy, outgoing queue, message/state subscriptions and open-waiters, calling validateOptions/mergeOptions, snapshot and exponentialBackoff along the way. It also defines the SocketView (read/send) and SocketController (lifecycle) interfaces and the createSocket factory that both the React layer and /core consumers use.

tour.title: Replaceable WebSocket Transport
tour.description: Underneath each logical connection sits a WebSocketTransport, which wraps a single native WebSocket with an immutable handshake configuration, forwards open/message/error/close events, and manages heartbeat pings and silence timeouts. Because transports are disposable and retired ones never call back, the LogicalConnection from Step 5 can swap them on reconnect or update without leaking stale events. This is the split between logical identity and physical transport that the README promises.

tour.title: SocketProvider and Global Sockets
tour.description: Moving into the React layer, SocketProvider.tsx builds a registry of LogicalConnections from registerSocket registrations, connecting them eagerly on mount and disposing them on unmount in a Strict-Mode-safe way. useGlobalSocket returns the shared read/send SocketView, while useGlobalSocketController returns the full SocketController for connect/reconnect/update/close; both resolve the connection through useProviderSocket. This split keeps ordinary consumers from accidentally driving lifecycle commands on a shared connection.
tour.languageLesson: React context lets a provider share one object (here a registry of connections) with any descendant without prop drilling. In React 18 Strict Mode, development builds mount, unmount and re-mount effects, so cleanup must be idempotent or deferred to avoid destroying a resource that is about to be reused.

tour.title: Component-Scoped Local Sockets
tour.description: useLocalSocket is the alternative to the Provider from Step 7: it calls createSocket to create a connection owned by a single component, connecting on mount and closing/disposing on unmount. Like the Provider, it uses deferred disposal so Strict Mode effect replays do not tear down and recreate the connection. Each hook owner gets an independent logical connection.

tour.title: Event, Send and State Hooks
tour.description: These small hooks work with any socket, global or local. useSocketEvent subscribes a handler to a typed message type (or wildcard) and keeps the latest handler in a ref to avoid resubscribing; useSocketSend returns a memoized send function; useSocketState exposes the ConnectionSnapshot from Step 4 through useSyncExternalStore. Together they turn the LogicalConnection's subscription API into idiomatic React.
tour.languageLesson: useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot) is React 18's tear-free way to read an external mutable store; getSnapshot must return a stable value between changes, which immutable snapshots provide. The 'latest ref' pattern stores a callback in useRef so an effect can call the newest handler without re-running.

tour.title: Test Suite
tour.description: The tests verify the guarantees described so far, backed by MockWebSocket, an EventTarget-based double that records sent payloads and simulates open, message and abnormal-close events. core.test.ts covers identity preservation across transport replacement, update coalescing, backoff, queue bounding, heartbeats and credential redaction; react.test.tsx checks Provider sharing, local socket identity and Strict Mode safety; types.test.ts uses expectTypeOf and @ts-expect-error to lock down the typed protocol from Step 3.
tour.languageLesson: Type-level tests guard generics at compile time: '@ts-expect-error' fails the build if the following line unexpectedly type-checks, and expectTypeOf asserts inferred types, so regressions in message typing surface during typechecking.

tour.title: Build and Tooling
tour.description: vite.config.ts builds the library in library mode with two entries (main index and React-free core) as ES and CJS bundles with React externalized, emits declarations via vite-plugin-dts from tsconfig.build.json, and runs Vitest in jsdom. tsconfig.build.json emits types only for the published sources and excludes tests, while the root tsconfig.json drives editor typechecking across src, tests and configs. This is how the two entry points from Step 2 become the published package.
tour.languageLesson: Externalizing peer dependencies such as React in a library build keeps them out of the bundle, so the consuming app supplies a single copy and avoids duplicate-React hook errors.
